newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi airline loses battle for survival.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi airline loses battle for survival.

text.p: New Zealand budget carrier Kiwi International collapsed on Monday after a young businessman failed in his David and Goliath battle with Australasia's most powerful airlines.
There is no connection between the New Zealand carrier and Newark, N.J.-based KIWI International Air Lines Inc.

Kiwi Chief Executive Ewan Wilson, a former travel agent who had taken on Qantas Airways and Air New Zealand in the cut-throat budget air travel market, admitted defeat after a series of crushing setbacks.

"We tried very, very hard to run an airline that was competitive and sustainable. I don't think we should hold our head low," the 30 year-old New Zealander said as he announced the airline's voluntary liquidation.

Operating with two leased aircraft, Kiwi ran up to 30 flights a week between New Zealand and Australia, but was hurt by severe competition, mechanical faults and flight disruptions from the eruption of Mount Ruapehu volcano in the North Island. The shutdown of Kiwi means the loss of more than 250 jobs.
The last straw was a legal dispute with Singapore's Region Air, lessor of an A320 Airbus that was grounded at Brisbane airport last week because of differences over lease terms.
Television New Zealand said those left stranded included a group of psychiatric patients and a brass band from Dunedin in the South Island.
Liquidator John Waller of Price Waterhouse said it was too early to comment on the size of Kiwi's debts.
